requirements.text: For vehicles with a lower bumper height at the test position of less than 425 mm, the requirements of paragraph 5.1.1. shall be applied.

For vehicles with a lower bumper height at the test position greater than, or equal to, 425 mm and less than 500 mm, the requirements of either paragraph 5.1.1. or 5.1.2., at the choice of the manufacturer, shall be applied.
For vehicles with a lower bumper height at the test position of greater than, or equal to, 500 mm, the requirements of paragraph 5.1.2. shall be applied.

When tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1. (Flexible lower legform impactor), the absolute value of the maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament elongation at the knee shall not exceed 22 mm.

When tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1. (Flexible lower legform impactor), the maximum dynamic anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament elongation shall not exceed 13 mm.
When tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1. (Flexible lower legform impactor), the absolute value of dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 340 Nm.
Where the manufacturer nominates bumper test widths up to a maximum of 264 mm in total, the absolute value of the tibia bending moment in those widths shall not exceed 380 Nm.
When tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 2. (upper legform to bumper), the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time shall not exceed 7.5 kN.
When tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 2. (upper legform to bumper), the bending moment on the test impactor shall not exceed 510 Nm.
All devices designed to protect vulnerable road users when impacted by the vehicle shall be correctly activated before and/or be active during the relevant test.
The international approval mark shall consist of a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The international approval mark shall consist of the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, to the right of the circle prescribed in paragraph 5.4.1.
After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3 to this Regulation, the vehicle shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 6.1.1. to 6.1.5.
After each impact test made in accordance with annex 3, the lighting and signalling devices shall continue to operate correctly and to remain visible.
After each impact test made in accordance with annex 3, the vehicle's bonnet (hood), boot lid (trunk lid) and doors shall be operable in the normal manner.
After each impact test made in accordance with annex 3, the vehicle's fuel and cooling systems shall have neither leaks nor constricted fluid passages which prevent normal functioning.
After each impact test made in accordance with annex 3, the sealing devices and caps of the vehicle's fuel and cooling systems shall be operable in the normal manner.

After each impact test made in accordance with annex 3, the vehicle's propulsion, suspension (including tyres), steering and braking systems shall remain in adjustment and shall operate in a normal manner; this requirement does not apply to sensors, cameras, radar devices, etc. being part of driver assist systems, which may become damaged, disoriented or broken due to an impact carried out according to Annex 3 as long as the basic braking and steering performance are still intact.
During the impact test the vehicle shall be at rest.
During the impact test the front wheels shall be in the straight-ahead position.
During the impact test the tyres shall be inflated to the pressure recommended by the vehicle manufacturer.
During the impact test the brakes shall be disengaged and the transmission control shall be in neutral position.

Vehicles equipped with hydro pneumatic, hydraulic or pneumatic suspension or a device for automatic levelling according to load shall be tested in the normal running conditions specified by the manufacturer.

In the two vehicle-loading conditions the protective device between the corners, as defined in paragraph 3.1.5. of this Regulation, shall be intersected by the horizontal plane passing through the reference line.

The external surface of the vehicle shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or any projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by the external surface or brushing against it in the event of a collision.
The external surface of the vehicle shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.

No protruding part of the external surface shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm, except that this requirement shall not apply to parts of the external surface which protrude less than 5 mm, whose outward facing angles shall however be blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.
The provisions of paragraphs 5.1. to 5.5. shall apply in addition to the particular specifications of paragraph 6., except where these particular specifications expressly provide otherwise.

Added ornaments which project more than 10 mm from their support shall retract, become detached or bend over under a force of 10 daN exerted at their most salient point in any direction in a plane approximately parallel to the surface on which they are mounted, except that this does not apply to ornaments on radiator grilles, to which only the general requirements of paragraph 5. apply.
After the added ornaments are retracted, detached or bent over, the remaining projections shall not project more than 10 mm.
The projections remaining after the added ornaments are retracted, detached or bent over shall in any case satisfy the provisions of paragraph 5.2.
Protective strips or shielding on the external surface shall be firmly secured to the vehicle.
For gaps of between 40 mm and 25 mm between consecutive elements of grilles and gaps, the radii of curvature shall be 1 mm or more.
If the distance between two consecutive elements of grilles and gaps is equal to or less than 25 mm, the radii of curvature of external faces of the elements shall not be less than 0.5 mm.
The junction of the front with the side faces of each element forming a grille or gap shall be blunted.

The ends of the bumpers shall be turned in towards the external surface in order to minimize the risk of fouling; this requirement is considered to be satisfied if either the bumper is recessed or integrated within the bodywork or the end of the bumper is turned in so that it is not contactable by a 100 mm sphere and the gap between the bumper end and the surrounding bodywork does not exceed 20 mm.

If the line of the bumper which corresponds to the outline contour of the car vertical projection is on a rigid surface, that surface shall have a minimum radius of curvature of 5 mm at all its points lying from the contour line to 20 mm inward, and a minimum radius of curvature of 2.5 mm in all other cases.
The provisions of paragraph 5. of this Regulation remain applicable to the bumper cover.

Supporting brackets provided by the vehicle manufacturer for registration plates shall comply with the requirements of paragraph 5.4. of this Regulation if they are contactable by a 100 mm diameter sphere when a registration plate is fitted in accordance with the vehicle manufacturer's recommendation.

Radio receiving and transmitting aerials shall be fitted to the vehicle in such a way that if their unattached end is less than 2 m from the road surface in any position of use specified by the manufacturer of the aerial, it shall be inside the zone bounded by the vertical planes which are 10 cm inside the extreme outer edge of the vehicle as defined in paragraph 2.7. of this Regulation.

Aerials shall be so fitted to the vehicle, and if necessary their unattached ends so restricted, that no part of the aerials protrude beyond the extreme outer edge of the vehicle as defined in paragraph 2.7. of this Regulation.
The bases of aerials shall not project more than 40 mm when determined according to the procedure of paragraph 2. of Annex 3 to this Regulation.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation and enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
It shall not be possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.

For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3° allowed in each direction.

The reference axis of the lamp shall be perpendicular to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle in the case of side retro-reflectors and of side-marker lamps and parallel to that plane in the case of all other signalling devices, with a tolerance of ±3° allowed in each direction.
Any specific instructions as regards fitting of the light-signalling devices laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall meet the conditions of paragraphs 5.5.1. to 5.5.5.

In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane (this estimate to be based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface referred to in paragraph 2.10.3.).

In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.

In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics, except that this shall not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.

In case of lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo shall be fitted on the rear of the vehicle and only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo shall be fitted on the front of the vehicle.
In case of lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, all logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos shall be prohibited.

Where lamps are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another, all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, shall be fulfilled.
The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed in such a way that either (a) the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis; these requirements do not apply to a single retro-reflector.

Two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be placed symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, extending on both sides to within at least 0.4 m of the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, and shall be not less than 0.8 m long.
The illumination of the surface of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be provided by not less than two light sources placed as close as possible to the ends.

Where the light-emitting surface of a band or strip lamp is constituted by a number of juxtaposed elements, these individual light-emitting surfaces, when projected on a transverse plane, shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of a lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.
Direction-indicator lamps, the vehicle-hazard warning signal, amber side-marker lamps complying with paragraph 6.18.7. below, and the emergency stop signal shall be flashing lamps.

Where the photometric characteristics of a lamp vary in relation to the ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, any variation in the photometric characteristics shall be in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
White light emitted by a lamp fitted on the front of the vehicle (as defined in paragraph 2.1.5.) shall not be visible from the rear of the vehicle.

For the visibility of white light towards the rear of a vehicle, with the exception of reversing lamps and white side conspicuity markings, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a white lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 2 in a transverse plane situated 25 m behind the vehicle (see Annex 4).

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
The concealment of lamps shall be prohibited, with the exception of the main-beam headlamps, the dipped-beam headlamps and the front fog lamps, which may be concealed when they are not in use.

The side-marker lamp shall emit amber light; however the rearmost side-marker lamp can be red if it is grouped or combined or reciprocally incorporated with the rear position lamp, the rear end-outline marker lamp, the rear fog lamp, the stop lamp or is grouped or has part of the light emitting surface in common with the rear retro-reflector.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.

With the exception of retro-reflectors, a lamp shall be capable of being made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse; otherwise, even if bearing an approval mark, it is deemed not to be present.

Lamps approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except when such light sources are used as non-replaceable light source(s) as defined in paragraph 2.9.1.2., shall be fitted in a vehicle in such a way that the light source can be correctly replaced without the need for expert assistance and without the need for special tools, other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.
Where a light source module includes a holder for an approved replaceable light source according to Regulation No. 37, this light source shall be replaceable as required in paragraph 5.23.

The voltage supplied at the terminals of devices which, according to their type approval documentation, have been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity, but no account is taken of obstacles if they were already present when the lamp was type-approved.

All lamps (devices) shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of this Regulation when installed on a vehicle.
In case of light-signalling lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.

Lamps installed on a vehicle which is approved according to this Regulation and approved for one or more replaceable light source categories according to Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128, shall be fitted with light sources approved according to these light source categories only; this requirement does not concern light source modules, LED modules and non-replaceable light sources, except for when they are required to be approved by the applicable Regulation.
The use of lamps approved for and equipped with LED substitute light source(s) is allowed exclusively in the case where the statement indicated in paragraph 3.2.8. is present and positive.
The SM1 type of side-marker lamp shall be used on all categories of vehicles; however the SM2 type of side-marker lamps may be used on the M1 category of vehicles.

On M1 and N1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length, side-marker lamps shall be used if they supplement the reduced geometric visibility of front position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.9.5.2. and rear position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.10.5.2.
The minimum number of side-marker lamps per side shall be such that the rules for longitudinal positioning are complied with.

The side-marker lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 91, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
The side-marker lamps shall be positioned in height above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm).

The side-marker lamps shall have a horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 45° to the front and to the rear; however for vehicles on which the installation of the side-marker lamps is optional this value can be reduced to 30°.

If the vehicle is equipped with side-marker lamps used to supplement the reduced geometric visibility of front and rear direction indicator lamps conforming to paragraph 6.5.5.2. and/or position lamps conforming to paragraphs 6.9.5.2. and 6.10.5.2., the horizontal angles of geometric visibility shall be 45° towards the front and rear ends of the vehicle and 30° towards the centre of the vehicle (see the figure in paragraph 6.5.5.2.).

The side-marker lamps shall have a vertical angle of geometric visibility of 10° above and below the horizontal; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
The side-marker lamps shall be oriented towards the side.

On M1 and N1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length, if amber side-marker lamps are wired to flash, the flashing shall be in phase and at the same frequency with the direction-indicator lamps at the same side of the vehicle.
An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation.
The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
The approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, to the right of the circle specified in paragraph 5.3.1.

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions, for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limits shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, and 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6 to this Regulation, and constant at 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7, and constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The transient conducted emission of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
For positive pulse polarity, the maximum allowed pulse amplitude of the ESA shall be +75 V for vehicles with 12 V systems and +150 V for vehicles with 24 V systems.
For negative pulse polarity, the maximum allowed pulse amplitude of the ESA shall be -100 V for vehicles with 12 V systems and -450 V for vehicles with 24 V systems.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.

The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type, tested by the method(s) described in Annex 9, shall meet the test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band given in Table 2a.

The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type, tested by the method(s) described in Annex 9, shall meet the test severity for the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band given in Table 2b.

For the ESA, the test level in over 90 per cent of the frequency range below 2 GHz shall be: stripline (20 to 400 MHz) 60 V/m; TEM cell (20 to 200 MHz) 75 V/m; BCI (20 to 400 MHz) 60 mA; ALSE (80 to 2,000 MHz) 30 V/m; reverberation chamber (LUF to 2,000 MHz) 21 V/m.

For the ESA, the test level in over 90 per cent of the frequency range above 2 GHz shall be: ALSE (2,000 to 6,000 MHz) 10 V/m; reverberation chamber (2,000 to 6,000 MHz) 7 V/m; not applicable for stripline, TEM cell and BCI.

For the ESA, the minimum test level over the whole frequency range below 2 GHz shall be: stripline (20 to 400 MHz) 50 V/m; TEM cell (20 to 200 MHz) 62,5 V/m; BCI (20 to 400 MHz) 50 mA; ALSE (80 to 2,000 MHz) 25 V/m; reverberation chamber (LUF to 2,000 MHz) 18 V/m.

For the ESA, the minimum test level over the whole frequency range above 2 GHz shall be: ALSE (2,000 to 6,000 MHz) 8 V/m; reverberation chamber (2,000 to 6,000 MHz) 6 V/m; not applicable for stripline, TEM cell and BCI.
The ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9.

The immunity of the ESA representative of its type to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
The starting profile shall be tested according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1.
The Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

For the starting profile, the ESA shall withstand immunity test level II for 12 V and 24 V systems, 10 pulses, with functional status B for ESA related to immunity related functions which shall be operational during engine start phases and C for other ESA, and D for ESA not related to immunity related functions.
For test pulse 1, the ESA shall withstand -75 V (12 V system) or -450 V (24 V system), 500 pulses, with FPSC III for ESA related and not related to immunity related functions.
For test pulse 2a, the ESA shall withstand +37 V (12 V and 24 V systems), 500 pulses, with FPSC I for ESA related to immunity related functions and III for ESA not related.
For test pulse 2b, the ESA shall withstand +10 V (12 V system) or +20 V (24 V system), 10 pulses, with FPSC II for ESA related to immunity related functions and III for ESA not related.
For test pulse 3a, the ESA shall withstand -112 V (12 V system) or -150 V (24 V system), for 1 h, with FPSC I for ESA related to immunity related functions and III for ESA not related.
For test pulse 3b, the ESA shall withstand +75 V (12 V system) or +150 V (24 V system), for 1 h, with FPSC I for ESA related to immunity related functions and III for ESA not related.
The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the measurement of radiated narrowband electromagnetic emissions.

ESAs complying with any combination of the test methods (absorber chamber ISO 11452-2, TEM cell ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection ISO 11452-4, stripline ISO 11452-5, reverberation chamber ISO 11452-11) at the manufacturer's discretion shall have the combination cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of this Annex.
The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
The test method shall ensure the immunity of ESAs to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
The test method shall limit conducted transients from ESAs to the vehicle power supply.

The test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The starting profile according to the International Standard ISO 16750-2 shall be applied to the supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines, except that ESAs that are exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor) are not subject to the starting profile.
The side marker lamp for all vehicle categories shall be identified by the symbol SM1 (paragraph 5.7.).
The side marker lamp for M1 vehicles shall be identified by the symbol SM2 (paragraph 5.7.).
Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
All markings shall be clearly legible and indelible.
With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for “a” shall be at least 5 mm (examples of the arrangement of the markings are shown in Annex 7).
The approval marking shall consist of the items listed in paragraphs 3.3.2.1. to 3.3.2.5.
The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The approval marking shall consist of the four to six-digit sequential number, being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The four to six-digit sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
The approval marking shall consist of the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
The approval marking shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
The approval marking shall include the additional symbol(s) of paragraphs 3.3.2.5.1. to 3.3.2.5.3., if applicable.
On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted shall be shown as an additional symbol.
Lamps shall bear the approval marking.
Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
Lamps, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.

Lamps shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage, in the case of lamps with (a) an electronic light source control gear; and/or (b) a variable luminous intensity control; and/or (c) a secondary operating mode; and/or (d) non-replaceable light sources.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module, comprising the starting letters “MD” for “MODULE” followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1., followed by additional symbols or characters in case several non-identical light source modules are used; the approval mark does not have to be the same as the one on the lamp in which the module is used, but both marks shall be from the same applicant.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii).
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.

An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.

In any case the approval marking as well as the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
If the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
In case an outer lens is used for several devices and bearing different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the component.
Where a single approval mark is affixed on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, it shall be visible after their installation.

Where a single approval mark is affixed on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.

The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
Each lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.

The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval shall apply to the lamp.

The requirements pertinent to each lamp and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the lamp is intended to be installed shall be applied, where its verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The lamps shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.

Where, on request of the applicant, the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) incorporates a manufacturer logo, it shall incorporate only one logo built by transparent or non-transparent components, and all requirements for the specific function of this Regulation shall be fulfilled, in addition to the conditions of paragraph 4.5.5. (a) to (d).

Where a logo is incorporated in a lamp, irrespective of the marking requirements in paragraph 3.3., only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer shall be allowed.

Where a logo is incorporated in a lamp, the enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm².

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the following shall apply: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced, in which case a note in the communication form states that the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.

The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128, provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval, and/or light source module(s) and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.

In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source(s) holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061; the holder data sheet relevant to the category of light source(s) prescribed applies and, where a category of LED substitute light source(s) is also prescribed, the holder data sheet relevant to the category of LED substitute light source(s) applies.
Light Signalling Devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances, which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position and can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it is tamperproof.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source and/or any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device shall be met.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall in no direction where the lamp is visible exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, outside the reference axis, either be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question, or be not less than the intensity value as specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
The provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed.
An interdependent lamp system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.

The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5. or exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5. for the specific lamp, as set out in paragraphs 4.8.3.4.1. and 4.8.3.4.2.
The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.

The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5. for the specific lamp, for systems depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, under night-time conditions.

The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5. for the specific lamp, for other systems, under standard conditions (good visibility, meteorological optical range MOR > 2,000 m, and clean lens).
Outside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3, no sharp variation of colour shall be observed.
The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of a side marker lamp (SM1, SM2) shall meet the requirements in Table 9.

(a)), a minimum of 6∙10⁻¹ cd within the standard light distribution of Figure A3-VII (par. 4.8.3.1. (c)), a maximum of 2.50∙10¹ cd (par. 4.8.3.1. (b)), and a minimum of 6∙10⁻¹ cd within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-3 (par. 4.8.3.1. (d)).

A side marker lamp of category SM2 shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 6∙10⁻¹ cd in the axis of reference (par. 4.8.3.1. (a)), a minimum of 6∙10⁻¹ cd within the standard light distribution of Figure A3-VIII (par. 4.8.3.1. (c)), a maximum of 2.50∙10¹ cd (par. 4.8.3.1. The side marker lamp shall meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.

The colour of the light emitted by a side marker lamp shall be amber; however, it can be red, if the rearmost side marker lamp is grouped or combined or reciprocally incorporated with the rear position lamp, the rear end-outline marker lamp, the rear fog lamp, the stop lamp, or is grouped with or has part of the light emitting surface in common with the rear retro-reflector.

Unless specified otherwise, the values shown in Figures A3-I to A3-XV give, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, which shall be mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.

In the case where a side marker lamp is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

Within the field of light distribution schematically shown as a grid, the light pattern should be substantially uniform, i.e. the light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value being shown on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction as a percentage.
Any approval marking arrangement other than the examples given shall be made in accordance with paragraph 3.3. of this Regulation.
For lamps (functions) using incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after photometric stability shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For all other lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution shall, in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at the point in time listed in Table A8-1.
The luminous intensity distribution of a side marker lamp shall be checked for compliance, in addition to paragraph 1, 4 seconds after switch ON at reference coordinate HV.

In case a lamp (function) uses any other light generating technology, the corresponding intensity requirements of the lamp (function) shall be tested and checked for compliance at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.

In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the corresponding minimum intensity requirements of a lamp (function) shall be tested and checked for compliance at all points in time starting at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.
